clue.text: Puny son, often washed out

definitions.note: a description, used as a noun phrase for underclothes that go through the wash regularly

parts.note: puny means small or slight
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A weak boy who is frequently pale and washed-out looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washed out' suggests a pale, feeble son, but it describes laundry: SMALLS is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is laundered so frequently that a description of constant washing stands for the garments themselves.

clue.text: Neat jelly at the bottom of the packet, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue the jelly piece sits below the packet piece

parts.note: a packet is a packet boat, an example of a ship, as 'perhaps' signals
a shape is an old word for a moulded jelly or blancmange

explanation.surface: A jelly found at the base of a parcel, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packet' suggests a parcel but is a mail boat; 'perhaps' marks it as one kind of ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and in good order, like a well-kept vessel.

clue.text: Pacify vegetarian animal

annotationWithheld.why: Pacify vegetarian animal (7): APPEASE is APE with PEAS inside, but 'vegetarian' must both supply PEAS and signal the insertion; no separate word gives the peas.

clue.text: Protection for the Chair from mudslingers?

definitions.text: Protection for the Chair from mudslingers?

parts.words: Protection for the Chair from mudslingers?
parts.note: the Chair sounds like a chairman under attack, but it is furniture shielded by a removable fitted fabric covering

explanation.surface: A chairman needs a shield against those who hurl abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Chair' suggests a person chairing a meeting and 'mudslingers' political smears; the protection is a fabric covering for an armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A removable fitted fabric covering keeps upholstery clean of muddy dirt.

clue.text: In confusion, lops head of everlasting flower

indicators.note: being in confusion means the letters of the following words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled gardener chops the top off an immortal bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In confusion' scrambles LOPS and HEAD together; 'lops head' looks like an instruction to behead a word, but nothing is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is the legendary flower of the Elysian Fields, a meadow bloom of the immortal dead, hence everlasting.

clue.text: Is sweet-bread a prominent feature in Brazil?

parts.note: sugar is the basic sweetener
a loaf is a unit of bread

explanation.surface: Is sweetbread a speciality of Brazilian cooking?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet-bread' looks like offal; split it into two. The mountain is the famous peak above Rio de Janeiro's harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The granite peak above Rio harbour is one of the country's best-known landmarks.

clue.text: Listen hard to chest

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Pay close attention to the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned command to hear or pay attention.

clue.text: Some men taken for a drink

definitions.meaning: in the board game ... the pieces are called men
a swallow or measure of liquid

explanation.surface: Several men are taken out for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers, whose pieces are men; the singular names one kind of piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulp of liquid; and a single checkers piece in British usage.

clue.text: Left sharp side of rock projecting

parts.note: edge is sharpness, as in a knife's edge

explanation.surface: A jagged flank of a crag juts out to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf jutting from a cliff face.

clue.text: Surgeon with nothing to say no to

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A surgeon with nothing to add refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or forbid a proposal by an authoritative refusal.

clue.text: Urchin learning to beg

parts.note: an urchin is a mischievous child, an imp
lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A street child picks up knowledge so as to plead for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly, the same as begging.

clue.text: Fish farming in bays

definitions.note: plural here, though the answer is singular: a wreath made of bay leaves

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
the land means farming as a way of life, as in working on the land

explanation.surface: Fish are being reared in coastal inlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bays' looks like sea inlets, but it means bay laurel leaves woven into a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of laurel (bay leaves) was the victor's crown, so a ring of bays is a festive wreath.

clue.text: Rollers bringing fish to the table

definitions.note: plural, though the answer is singular: the board rides on wheels

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish
board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Waiters wheel a fish dish over to the diners' table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rollers' suggests waves or hair curlers; here it is a board on small wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled deck that a rider stands on rolls along, so it can be called a roller.

clue.text: Sir Andrew's sort of impudence gives one a fit

definitions.meaning: Sir Andrew Aguecheek in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night: his cheek, a word for impudence, is the first half of his surname
a bout of fever with violent shivering

explanation.surface: A knight's insolence is enough to make someone have a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: Impudence is cheek, and Sir Andrew Aguecheek of Twelfth Night has that particular kind of cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarial fever comes in shivering attacks, each one a fit.

clue.text: Praiseworthy arrangement to clear one debt

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of the words into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deal made to pay off a single debt deserves praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like a financial deal but shuffles CLEAR, I and DEBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving credit or commendation.

clue.text: Sound pitch, but on one spot it's getting thinner

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: an ace on a die or card has a single pip
tone is the pitch or quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A singer's note is good, but at a single spot it becomes weaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting thinner' suggests something diminishing; read 'thinner' as a noun, a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile solvent is used to dilute paints and remove varnish, the job of a paint thinner.

clue.text: Soldier wouldn't look right obeying this order

definitions.text: Soldier wouldn't look right obeying this order

parts.words: Soldier wouldn't look right obeying this order
parts.note: a drill command telling troops to stop looking to the side and face ahead, so they no longer look right

explanation.surface: A soldier who follows this command would appear out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wouldn't look right' seems to mean appear wrong; it means not turn the head to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The parade-ground word of command that returns troops' gaze ahead after a turn of the head.

clue.text: Field force unit concealed in E Dorset

indicators.note: the letters are disguised within the place name, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; East Dorset is a district in south-west England

explanation.surface: A military field unit lies hidden in East Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field force unit' reads as soldiers, but it is a unit of magnetic field strength; 'concealed in' looks like a hidden-word signal, yet the letters must be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Danish physicist, the oersted measures magnetising field intensity in the CGS system.

clue.text: Application for a stage-coach

explanation.surface: Someone applies to ride on a stagecoach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' suggests a form; it means persistent effort. The second sense is the French word for a horse-drawn stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Industriousness; and the old French public coach.

clue.text: He interprets outdated notes about contract

parts.note: ex means former or no longer current

indicators.note: the notes go round the word for contract, enclosing it

parts.note: E is a musical note; two of them give the plural
to get an illness is to contract it

explanation.surface: Someone who explains old memos about an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a legal agreement, but it is the verb, as in catching a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete is a scholar who expounds and explains texts, especially scripture.

clue.text: Not changing uniform

explanation.surface: Garments that stay the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing but is the adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and even in temper or conditions.

clue.text: Feared movement to the left of central government

indicators.note: to joins the next piece on after the anagram
movement means the letters of feared are shifted around

explanation.surface: A frightening shift leftwards in the government at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement to the left' looks like politics, but 'movement' stirs FEARED and L for 'left' is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: In a federation the national authority, as opposed to the states, is the federal power.

clue.text: Abusive language from a fence

definitions.meaning: a barrier of bars or posts

explanation.surface: Insults shouted from over a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranting scornfully; and a barrier of upright bars.

clue.text: Guide pointing to the light

definitions.meaning: a hint or indication that leads someone to an answer
in crossword terms a light is a grid entry, and each one has a hint pointing to it

explanation.surface: A guide shows the way towards illumination.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' is the crosswording word for an answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint guides a solver, and each grid entry has its own printed hint.

clue.text: Professed faith in sacred offerings

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words sacred offerings

explanation.surface: Religious belief expressed through holy gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of belief, such as the Creed recited in church.

clue.text: Cricket side delicately tapping the ball — how disconcerting!

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
in golf, putting is gently tapping the ball towards the hole

explanation.surface: A cricketer softly taps the ball on the off side, which is unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR garbled the line breaks; the page reads 'tapping' and 'disconcerting'. The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsettling or discouraging is said to put people off.

clue.text: Fish look sullen

definitions.meaning: a kind of fish, the whiting-... or bib
to push out the lips in sulky displeasure

explanation.surface: A fish wears a sulky expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cod-family fish; and sticking out the lips in sulkiness.

clue.text: Brother to Uncle Remus

parts.note: the dialect title for 'brother' used by the storyteller in Joel Chandler Harris's tales, as with the Rabbit and the Fox

explanation.surface: A sibling of the storyteller Uncle Remus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother to' looks like family; it means the word for brother as Uncle Remus says it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect form of brother in the Uncle Remus folk tales.

clue.text: Stop, change to amber, then green

indicators.note: then puts the next piece after the anagram
change means the letters of amber are reordered

parts.note: a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Traffic lights cycle from halt through amber to green.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic-light picture of stop, amber, green is a disguise: 'Stop' is the definition and 'change' shuffles AMBER into EMBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade halts it, so a ban is a stop.

clue.text: University man accepts married Italian

indicators.note: the university man takes in another letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: Brian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A graduate fellow takes on a wedded Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' stands for a man's name, BRIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a region of central Italy, so a native of it is an Italian.

clue.text: Put too much value on speed of deliveries

definitions.meaning: to esteem something more highly than it deserves
in cricket, the ... is how quickly a side bowls its overs

explanation.surface: Someone prizes the swiftness of parcel couriers excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels; in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and the over rate measures how fast overs are got through.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize beyond merit is to overvalue; the cricket term counts overs bowled per hour.

clue.text: Blackbird used to chase hares

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A blackbird was employed to pursue hares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blackbird' splits into B for black and a bird; the definition describes a hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This small hound was bred for hunting hares on foot.
